issues.claim: R2-26 (a) put a raised way's ring-end foot on ground part 0's `margin` chain (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`, l. 2296–2299: 'its ground end a `raised_foot` vertex placed by `splitThrough` on ground part 0's `margin` chain at the deck's end point … no ramp or stair is drawn there'). It hands the frame growth to 'the raised way's re-derivation re-placing both ends of that foot on the new rings'. The kernel's frame growth runs first and leaves the vertex undefined. Batch (b) on part 0 (§3.2 (9), l. 3563–3566) strips the old ring's `margin` rows, and 'a stretch left with no row is deleted'. At a ring-end foot, part 0 carries no ramp and no way, so the foot's vertex loses both its edges and keeps only its `raised_foot` row. §3.2 (9)'s vertex rule (l. 3573) says such a vertex 'stays'. But the arena's vertex record has `out: one outgoing half-edge` (§2.2, l. 592), and no text defines a vertex with no edge. §2.2 rule 3's dissolution covers only degree-2 vertices, and §3.4's strip of a far end 'restores the edge it split', which is gone. The raised part's own end is an antenna end of its spine, as a through-road's is; part 0's end is not. Between the growth and §4.11's re-derivation, part 0 therefore holds a vertex the kernel cannot represent, and the walks, the index, §3.10's rows and its later removal are undefined there. This is canon's named combination C-raised-frame (edges.json, UNDEFINED), opened by this round's foot on the ring (principle (11)).
issues.required_change: §3.2 (9): after 'A vertex of an old chain that keeps a row or another edge stays — a through-road's end on the old ring is an antenna end until §4.11 continues its way — and every other dissolves or stays by §2.2 rule 3.' add: 'A raised way's ground foot at a deck end on the old ring (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`) — a `raised_foot` vertex the strip would leave with its row and no edge — is never left so. On part 0, batch (b)'s insertion (the new ring with S1's water) and its strip are then two L0 batches, and between them one batch at the foot row's level moves each such foot: its row is stripped by `removeEdges` on its `VertexRef`, the vertex dissolving back into the old ring (§2.2 rule 3), and added by `splitThrough` on the new ring at that ring's point nearest it (ties by lattice address). The deck end on the raised part's own old ring stays an antenna end of its spine, as a through-road's end does. The raised way's re-derivation (§4.11) then extends the deck to the new ring and re-places both ends of that foot (§2.7), so both ends resolve at every stage end (§3.10's stored-references row).' In (b) itself, replace '`Plat.frame` takes the new frame as this batch commits' with '`Plat.frame` takes the new frame as its last batch commits'. (Another shape is acceptable, e.g. a defined isolated vertex with `out` = −1 that the re-derivation deletes, provided both ends resolve at every stage end; VKr2-02 tests it.)

issues.claim: No bar exercises VKr2-01's case: a raised way whose deck ends on the outer ring, carried through an epoch's frame growth. T110-2 (§13.2, l. 17982–17985) builds 'its part sized to the ground's frame plus margin and growing with it' and 'an aqueduct sourced beyond the frame laid to the outer ring without a ramp' as separate clauses. §13.1's kernel set (l. 17186–17190) grows a frame only in 'a frame growth whose frame and arena would be no larger' and 'a village → town fold'. Nothing checks the foot through the growth: it must resolve at every stage end, the old ground vertex must leave nothing behind, and both ends must lie on the new rings after §4.11. Under principle (11) an untested edge is a major.
issues.required_change: §13.2 T110-2: after 'an aqueduct sourced beyond the frame laid to the outer ring without a ramp,' add 'and the same aqueduct through an epoch's frame growth — §3.10's stored-references row passing at every stage end of the epoch, no part-0 vertex left with a row and no edge, and after §4.11 both ends of its ring-end foot on the new rings (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`, §3.2 (9)) —'.

issues.claim: §3.1's code list (l. 3450) gives `'E_NO_PATH' // with the closest reached point [F-ROUTE]`. The bracket names the classes the code reaches, as the brackets of `E_KEPT`, `E_LEVEL` and `E_SELF_INTERSECT` name the dry run. Pipeline's round-2 text (VPC-R1-23) in II.7.6 step 3 (l. 21252–21256) now routes the same code elsewhere: 'a route the search does not find (`E_NO_PATH`, §3.1 …): the dry run refuses with its reason … (F-EDIT, §5.2)'. At generation, the connection stage runs the same connector for an undercity lifeline (§7.3 item 9 (d)'s *At generation*, l. 10932–10934). A neighbourhood whose lifeline finds no route is F-VOID's 'a neighbourhood left without a lifeline' (§5.2, l. 8978). The code's home thus names one consumer of three.
issues.required_change: §3.1, l. 3450: replace '// with the closest reached point [F-ROUTE]' with '// with the closest reached point [F-ROUTE; F-VOID — an undercity lifeline's dug connector at generation, II.7.5, II.7.6; in an edit the dry run's refusal, F-EDIT — II.7.6 step 3]'.

issues.claim: II.7.6 step 3's new refusal (l. 21252–21256, VPC-R1-23), for a dug connector the path search cannot route, 'naming the blocking building or the water table (F-EDIT, §5.2)', has no row in §7.1's outcome table. §5.2 F-EDIT detects 'every refusal and conflict cause of §7.1's dry-run outcome table', and §7.1 calls the table 'the one home of every refusal, conflict and bend cause of a dry run'. Yet the table's `addUndergroundAccess` row (l. 10380) covers only 'terrain rules out every basement form … or whose connector passes its route's bound (II.7.6)'. So the refusal has no catalogue key or action. repair-r2-pipeline.md lists this as a HAND-OFF for round 3 that no repair applied; T66-2 (l. 17740–17747) already tests the outcome.
issues.required_change: §7.1's outcome table, the `addUndergroundAccess` row: replace 'or whose connector passes its route's bound (II.7.6)' with 'or whose connector passes its route's bound or finds no route (II.7.6 step 3, `E_NO_PATH`)'; in its actions cell, replace 'else the refusal naming the terrain or the route's bound' with 'else the refusal naming the terrain, the route's bound, or the building or water table that blocks the route'.

issues.claim: §4.3 *Raised ways* (l. 5572–5573) still reads 'its two ends are ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices — each of its two feet a vertex on part 0 joined by record to one on its part (§3.4) —'. R2-26 (a) makes §2.7's `RaisedWayRecord.feet` the one statement, which §3.4 and §4.1 now cite without restating. §2.7's opening line (l. 2510) now adds 'or an end on the arena's outer ring'. §4.3 thus restates the feet, leaves out the ring end, and cites §3.4 rather than the record's home. It is the same defect as VKr1-04.
issues.required_change: §4.3: replace 'its two ends are ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices — each of its two feet a vertex on part 0 joined by record to one on its part (§3.4) —,' with 'its two ends are its feet on ground part 0 (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7),'.

issues.claim: §7.1's `drawWay` comment (l. 10073) reads 'raised?: true /* item 110 (b): the deck in its own ground arena part (§3.4), its two ends ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices, …'. A drawn raised course beyond the frame is bent to the ring (§2.7 *At the frame*, item 101 R2), and that end carries no ramp or stair (`RaisedFoot`). The comment contradicts the one statement R2-26 (a) rules.
issues.required_change: §7.1 `drawWay`: replace 'its two ends ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices' with 'its two ends its feet (§2.7's `RaisedWayRecord.feet`)'.

issues.claim: V05 §3 (d) (V05 l. 1687) argues 'No raised way reaches an island' from the premise 'A raised part's two ends are ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices (item 110 (b))'. That premise restates §2.7 without its ring-end foot (R2-26 (a)). The conclusion holds either way, since every foot lies on ground part 0.
issues.required_change: V05 l. 1687: replace 'A raised part's two ends are ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices (item 110 (b))' with 'A raised part's two ends are its feet on ground part 0 (§2.7's `RaisedWayRecord.feet`; item 110 (b))'.

issues.claim: Round 2's §11.2 `apply` signature (R2-42) has `onProgress` for a `'undo'` wait (l. 15850): 'a group of `undo` or `redo` events, its events undone or redone of the total (V09 §4.21.9, §3.9)'. Under canon S7 the bare §3.9 reads as the kernel's *Geometry in the document*, which says nothing of undo progress. The meant section is V09 §3.9 *Undo, redo, restore points and "open a copy from here"* (V09 l. 1312). It is the list-continuation class of VKr1-08, new this round.

V04's round-2 damage rows (item 123) name `bandUnion` for underground bands in two places. The `cellarWall` kind (V04 l. 2886) reads 'an underground building's wall run on a footprint side that lies on its part's rock (outside the part's `bandUnion`, §3.7)'. The read map (V04 l. 308) reads 'each underground building's footprint sides on its part's rock (§3.7's `bandUnion`)'. But §3.7 gives `bandUnion` the wall bands, glacis, tower and gatehouse footprints (l. 4440–4441). A tunnel's or gallery's band — bore plus wall, whose outer ring is the kerb — is committed by `corridorUnion` (§3.7, l. 4445–4451; §2.2 rule 1's underground parts; V04's own l. 1135 and l. 2010). The rows name the wrong kernel function for the band a footprint side is tested against.
issues.required_change: V04 l. 2886: replace '(outside the part's `bandUnion`, §3.7)' with '(off its tunnel's or gallery's band, which `corridorUnion` commits, §3.7)'. V04 l. 308: replace '(§3.7's `bandUnion`)' with '(off the bands `corridorUnion` commits, §3.7)'.
